primary_antecedent.scope: Condition P, coisotropic characteristic saturation, maximal-interval homogeneous normal forms and escaping versus persistent regular characteristics.

source_correspondence: Condition P uses both orientations and all smooth nonzero multipliers on the exact real zero level. The antipodal anti-symplectic identity proves the differential-operator necessity consequence.

Independent real differentials give the rank-two coisotropic set. An actual compact ordinary Hamiltonian tube and sign-preserving integral division give f=g*h on one common product, with h nonnegative and dg nonzero.

Every semibicharacteristic meeting the rank-two set remains characteristic. The exact saturation equality includes both set inclusions, product-boundary exclusion, nonvanishing multiplier interpolation and continuation to a contradictory noncharacteristic slice.

The saturation is locally closed, embedded, codimension two and conic. Its complete characteristic foliation comes from exact current flow and maximal-leaf providers. No global Hausdorff or Riemann quotient is inferred.
A nonextendible regular endpoint excludes radial motion and repeated cosphere points. Exact compact homogeneous normal-form providers give the full transverse-independent temporal momentum reduction.

Inside the saturation, a nearby rank-two time supplies homogeneous nonnegative factorization. Outside it, a noncharacteristic time and condition P supply a common weak sign. The regular point versions and all conic degrees are retained.

Escaping characteristic components and persistent regular curves are distinguished. Geometric continuation is asserted only in the regular open locus, without an unsupported completeness claim for a rescaled field.

Three complete solutions give the flat plateau saturation and complex invariant, a Psi symbol failing P in one cone, and a semidefinite rank-changing Hessian. The last example proves P for every multiplier by invariant-submanifold uniqueness.

Indefinite quadratic division and the affine clock and semidefinite division with a nonnegative quotient treat the quadratic alternatives. The sign-based energy estimate connects this geometry to directed propagation. The rank-changing semidefinite obstruction retains its stated scope.

For a jointly real analytic sign-coherent normal-form function,AF0 gives a time-independent analytic factor and one nonnegative jointly analytic quotient on a neighborhood of the whole compact interval. Its proof includes analytic division,preparation,factorization of real analytic germs and a regular-root parity argument.

Ordinary analytic sign factorization permits the quotient to vanish on the central characteristic. The analytic changing-rank example X3 excludes a time-independent factor with nonzero quotients at both marked N12 endpoints.
